questions.q: Why can't a GitHub Actions runner authenticate to Salesforce using sf org login web?
options: sf org login web is deprecated and no longer exists
A CI runner is a disposable machine with no browser a human can interact with, so interactive login can't work there
GitHub Actions blocks all Salesforce domains by default
sf org login web only works with sandboxes, never production
questions.explain: sf org login web requires a human to interact with a browser login prompt -- something a disposable, non-interactive CI runner has no way to provide.

questions.q: In the JWT Bearer flow, which half of the RSA key pair is uploaded to the Connected App in Salesforce Setup?
options: The private key
Neither -- Salesforce generates its own key pair automatically
The GitHub repository's SSH key
The certificate (public key)
questions.explain: The certificate (public key) is uploaded to the Connected App's digital signature setting; the private key stays only in GitHub as a secret, never in Salesforce.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four GitHub secrets this lesson lists for JWT-based CI authentication?
options: SF_PASSWORD
SF_CLIENT_ID
SF_PRIVATE_KEY
SF_INSTANCE_URL
questions.explain: The four secrets are SF_CLIENT_ID, SF_PRIVATE_KEY, SF_USERNAME, and SF_INSTANCE_URL -- JWT auth uses a signed key, not a password, so there is no SF_PASSWORD secret.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend a dedicated integration user rather than a real administrator's own username for pipeline authentication?
options: Because real administrators cannot be authenticated via JWT at all
Because integration users run Apex tests faster
Because a dedicated integration user created specifically for the pipeline keeps pipeline access separate from any individual person's own login
There is no stated reason in this lesson
questions.explain: A dedicated integration user isolates pipeline access from any one person's credentials, so the pipeline's access doesn't depend on -- or get entangled with -- a real person's own account.

questions.q: Why is the JWT Bearer flow considered safer for a shared pipeline than storing a single SFDX auth URL as one secret?
options: Because JWT separates the private key and the Connected App into two independently revocable pieces, letting you rotate the certificate without touching the integration user's credentials, unlike a bare session URL
Because the auth URL is actually more secure, just slower to set up
Because the SFDX auth URL cannot be used in GitHub Actions at all
Because JWT requires no secrets to be stored anywhere
questions.explain: The auth URL is itself a live session credential with no independent rotation mechanism, while JWT's key pair and Connected App can be managed and revoked separately.
